injuryReports.returnComment: Aubrey was able to convert multiple field-goal tries for the third straight game, but he did miss a kick for the second straight week. The kicker had makes from 45 and 28 yards in the contest, but he continued his long-range struggles Sunday, pulling a 50-yard attempt wide left late in the fourth quarter. Aubrey has now gone 17-for-22 on field-goal tries, including 3-for-8 from 50-plus yards, over nine contests to open the 2026 campaign.
injuryReports.injury: Aubrey went 2-for-3 on field-goal attempts and made all three of his PATs during Sunday's 27-23 win over the Colts.

injuryReports.name: Dak Prescott
injuryReports.returnComment: Prescott had a couple of bumps in the road against an inconsistent Colts defense, but the veteran signal-caller, who was also working without George Pickens (hamstring), still found his way to his third 300-yard effort of the season. Prescott unsurprisingly bestowed plenty of attention on CeeDee Lamb, who ultimately was responsible for 10 of his completions, 195 of his yards and one of his two TDs. Prescott also connected with Jake Ferguson for a 10-yard scoring strike early in the second quarter, and the one blemish on the star quarterback's day was a  fumble on a sack at his own 16-yard line that led to a Colts touchdown. Prescott has at least one touchdown pass in every game heading into a Week 10 home showdown against the 49ers next Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Prescott completed 21 of 34 passes for 335 yards with two touchdowns and no interceptions while rushing twice for one yard in the Cowboys' 27-23 win over the Colts on Sunday. He also lost a fumble.

injuryReports.name: Javonte Williams
injuryReports.returnComment: Williams turned in one of his more efficient performances against an inconsistent Colts defense, ultimately managing his second 100-yard effort of the season. Williams continued to serve as a prolific supplier of touchdowns as well, recording his ninth rushing score of the campaign on a one-yard run with 1:08 remaining to seal the victory for Dallas. Williams' week-to-week yardage production has fluctuated a fair amount, but his high-volume role and trusted red-zone presence keeps him a must-play despite a tough Week 10 home matchup against the 49ers next Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Williams rushed 20 times for 101 yards and a touchdown and brought in four of five targets for 23 yards in the Cowboys' 27-23 win over the Colts on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: CeeDee Lamb
injuryReports.returnComment: Lamb easily led the Cowboys across the board in receptions, receiving yards and targets in a game that Dallas was operating without George Pickens (hamstring). Lamb's yardage total was a new season high, and he rounded out his stellar day with his seventh touchdown catch of the campaign on a 44-yard grab just before halftime. Even his turnover had a bright side to it from a fantasy perspective, as Lamb gained 44 yards on an impressive downfield catch and picked up extra yardage after the Colts initially failed to touch him down before fumbling at the end of that sequence. Lamb has four straight double-digit target games and is just 96 yards away from his sixth consecutive 1,000-yard season heading into a Week 10 home showdown against the 49ers next Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Lamb brought in 10 of 16 targets for 195 yards and a touchdown in the Cowboys' 27-23 win over the Colts on Sunday. He also lost a fumble.

injuryReports.name: Dee Winters
injuryReports.returnComment: Winters was evaluated for a concussion earlier in the second half but was ultimately cleared to return. That's a big boost to Dallas' defense, especially since fellow linebacker DeMarvion Overshown (hamstring/back) was unable to suit up Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Winters (head) has returned to Sunday's Week 9 matchup against the Colts, Patrik Walker of the Cowboys' official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Jonathan Mingo
injuryReports.returnComment: Mingo was hurt in the second half and may not be able to return to the game. Prior to his exit, he caught one of three targets for 23 yards. With George Pickens (hamstring) and KaVontae Turpin (ribs) inactive Sunday, the Cowboys will be down to CeeDee Lamb, Ryan Flournoy, Camden Brown and Jordan Hudson at wideout if Mingo can't return.

injuryReports.name: Marist Liufau
injuryReports.returnComment: Liufau broke his left forearm in the Cowboys' preseason finale against the Saints and has yet to play in the 2026 regular season. The linebacker is set to make his debut in Sunday's contest after being activated from IR on Saturday.
injuryReports.injury: Liufau (forearm) is active for Sunday's game against the Colts.

injuryReports.name: Jonathan Bullard
injuryReports.returnComment: Bullard had his practice window opened Oct. 29 and was a full participant in all three of the Cowboys' practices this week. However, he's not yet ready to return to game action. Bullard's next chance to suit up is Sunday, Nov. 15, against San Francisco.

injuryReports.name: Malachi Lawrence
injuryReports.returnComment: Lawrence suffered an ankle injury last Sunday in a loss to Arizona and had already been ruled out for Week 9. The move to IR means he'll need to miss at least three additional games, so the earliest Lawrence can return is Monday, Dec. 7, against Seattle. The Cowboys activated fellow linebacker Marist Liufau (forearm) from IR on Saturday to fill Lawrence's roster spot.

injuryReports.name: Tyler Smith
injuryReports.returnComment: Smith upgraded to a full participant in Friday's practice after being limited in consecutive sessions to start Week 9 prep. The star left guard is all set to suit up for Sunday's contest to defend Dak Prescott against the Colts' pass rush.
injuryReports.injury: Smith (ankle) does not have any injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Colts, Tommy Yarrish of the Cowboys' official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Chuck Clark
injuryReports.returnComment: Clark jumped in front of a Malik Willis (abdomen) deep pass intended for Caleb Douglas early in the third quarter, which the Lions offense converted into a 33-yard field goal by Jake Bates eight plays later. It was Clark's second interception of the season and first since Week 1 against the Saints. The veteran safety is up to 49 tackles (28 solo), including 1.0 sacks, three pass defenses and one forced fumble through eight regular-season games.
injuryReports.injury: Clark registered five tackles (three solo) and one interception during the Lions' 19-9 win over the Dolphins in Week 9.

injuryReports.name: D.J. Reed
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable

injuryReports.name: Kerby Joseph
injuryReports.returnComment: The Lions opened Joseph's 21-day practice window to return from the PUP list two weeks ago, so they have just one week to activate him before they'd be required to put him back on the shelf for the rest of the season. He's already been ruled out for Sunday's game versus the Patriots, but managing a full practice Thursday or Friday would still probably go a long way toward convincing the team he's ready for game action again.

injuryReports.name: Brian Branch
injuryReports.returnComment: Branch played all 57 of the Lions' defensive snaps in Week 9, and the fact that he was present for Wednesday's practice session suggests his injury is likely not overly severe. If he can upgrade to full participation at practice Thursday or Friday, there's a good chance he'll avoid carrying an injury designation into the weekend.

injuryReports.name: Jacob Saylors
injuryReports.returnComment: Saylors sat out his first game of the season in Week 9 due to a neck injury, but it now looks like he's on track to return to game action in Week 10. With teammate Sione Vaki tending to an ankle issue, it appears possible Saylors could be called upon for a larger share of offensive snaps than usual versus the Patriots.
injuryReports.injury: Saylors (neck) was a full participant at practice Wednesday.

injuryReports.name: Sione Vaki
injuryReports.returnComment: Vaki played 20 offensive snaps during Sunday's game at Miami, and it seems like he may have hurt his ankle at some point along the way. He'll probably have to return to practice Thursday or Friday to have a realistic chance of suiting up in Week 10 versus the Patriots.

injuryReports.name: Jared Goff
injuryReports.returnComment: Goff is making his first appearance on the injury report this season, but he at least logged some reps Wednesday as he tends to a health concern. A return to full participation Thursday and/or Friday should put him in the clear for Sunday's game versus the Patriots.

injuryReports.name: Amon-Ra St. Brown
injuryReports.returnComment: St. Brown also was limited on all three of the Lions' Week 9 practice reports due to a rib injury, but he was able to suit up this past Sunday at Miami and log a typical 75 percent snap share en route to eight catches (on 10 targets) for 86 yards. Friday's injury report will determine if he enters the weekend with a designation for Sunday's game against the Patriots.

injuryReports.name: Isaac TeSlaa
injuryReports.returnComment: Jared Goff threw to TeSlaa twice on Detroit's opening drive but didn't turn to him again for the remainder of the contest. The second-year wideout thus continued a very unproductive stretch, as he's logged just two catches for 19 yards on six targets over his past four games. TeSlaa is still working as Detroit's No. 3 wideout -- among Lions wide receivers, only Jameson Williams and Amon-Ra St. Brown logged more offensive snaps Sunday -- but looks just aren't coming his way. He'll try to break out of the funk next Sunday against New England.
injuryReports.injury: TeSlaa registered one catch for nine yards on two targets in Sunday's 19-9 win over Miami.

injuryReports.name: Sam LaPorta
injuryReports.returnComment: Earlier in the season, LaPorta expressed his frustration with the Lions for the organization's inability to come to terms on an extension with him, but both sides still appear to be on good terms and willing to re-engage in discussions on a new deal before he becomes a free agent in 2027. The fourth-year tight end has likely helped his case for earning a lucrative contract by having thus far stayed healthy throughout the season while putting together a 35-399-3 receiving line on 49 targets over the Lions' first eight games.
injuryReports.injury: The Lions have received trade calls on LaPorta leading up to Tuesday's deadline, but the team prefers to keep him with the hope of signing the tight end to a long-term deal, Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.com reports.

injuryReports.name: DJ Wonnum
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable

injuryReports.name: Cade Mays
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable

injuryReports.name: Andre Cisco
injuryReports.returnComment: Cisco will now suit up for his third NFL team after spending time with the Jaguars and Jets since entering the league in 2021. In 80 regular-season games, the 26-year-old has accumulated 293 total tackles (197 solo), including 2.5 sacks, and four forced fumbles. Although Detroit expects Kerby Joseph (knee) to be back on the field soon, Cisco will provide much-needed depth at the safety position.
injuryReports.injury: The Lions acquired Cisco from the Jets on Monday in exchange for a 2028 sixth-round pick, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.

injuryReports.name: Jake Bates
injuryReports.returnComment: Bates was able to make multiple field goals for the third straight game after having done so just once over the team's first five contests this year. The kicker converted attempts from 28 and 40 yards in the first half before adding makes from 33 and 43 yards after the break. Bates has now gone 16-for-17 on field-goal tries while making all 24 of his PATs over eight games during the 2026 campaign to this point.
injuryReports.injury: Bates went 4-for-4 on field-goal attempts and made his only extra-point try during Sunday's 19-9 win over the Dolphins.

injuryReports.name: Jameson Williams
injuryReports.returnComment: Williams and the rest of the Lions' air attack had a quiet afternoon, as Jared Goff threw for just 170 yards overall. Williams was efficient on his two touches, but he finished with a new season low in receiving yards. The 2022 first-round pick, who's averaging 16.7 yards per reception on the season, will likely be busier in a Week 10 matchup against the Patriots in Germany next Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Williams brought in one of two targets for 31 yards and rushed once for nine yards in the Lions' 19-9 win over the Dolphins on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Jahmyr Gibbs
injuryReports.returnComment: It was a relatively quiet day by Gibbs' lofty standards against a Dolphins team that's proven to have plenty of fight despite its losing record. The standout back salvaged his fantasy day with an eight-yard touchdown run late in the third quarter, Gibbs' second score on the ground in as many games and ninth overall. Gibbs failed to record at least one reception for the first time this season, but he's already amassed 1,132 scrimmage yards and 11 total touchdowns across eight games heading into next Sunday's showdown against the Patriots in Germany.
injuryReports.injury: Gibbs rushed 20 times for 74 yards and a touchdown and failed to bring in his only target in the Lions' 19-9 win over the Dolphins on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Jack Campbell
injuryReports.returnComment: Campbell suffered a neck injury while making a tackle in the third quarter of last Sunday's win over Minnesota and remains in the hospital. Detroit head coach Dan Campbell shared Friday that the linebacker continues to improve, but  his placement on IR means he'll miss at least the team's next four games. K.J. Britt, who Detroit signed off New England's practice squad Wednesday, may be asked to immediately step into a starting role.

injuryReports.name: Jimmy Rolder
injuryReports.returnComment: This move was anticipated, as Rolder suffered a season-ending hamstring injury in the Lions' win over Minnesota on Sunday. The rookie linebacker logged a career-high 17 defensive snaps and notched his first NFL sack in that contest, so his injury comes at an unfortunate time. Rolder will now turn his focus toward rehabbing the injury in order to be ready for offseason activities in 2027.

injuryReports.name: Roger McCreary
injuryReports.returnComment: McCreary wasn't listed on the injury report Wednesday or Thursday but practiced in a limited capacity Friday. As a result, the 26-year-old was listed as questionable for the divisional showdown with Minnesota, though he has since been cleared to suit up. McCreary has appeared in all six of Detroit's regular-season games in 2026, amassing 22 total tackles (17 solo), 1.0 sacks and one forced fumble.
injuryReports.injury: McCreary (foot) is active for Sunday's game against the Vikings.

injuryReports.name: Ennis Rakestraw Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: Rakestraw suffered an ankle injury late in this past Sunday's win over Green Bay. He was held to limited practice sessions Wednesday and Thursday but was able to upgrade to full participation Friday. As such, Rakestraw is good to go for Sunday's big battle against Minnesota.
injuryReports.injury: Rakestraw (ankle) does not have a game designation for Sunday's Week 8 tilt versus the Vikings.

injuryReports.name: Isiah Pacheco
injuryReports.returnComment: Pacheco has been sidelined for the entirety of the regular season to this point after undergoing back surgery in September. Sione Vaki has been working as the Lions' clear RB2, though Jahmyr Gibbs has been a true workhorse out of the backfield. If Pacheco does return at the end of the regular season, it's hard to envision him having a big impact coming off back surgery.

injuryReports.name: Josh Jacobs
injuryReports.returnComment: Jacobs exited Green Bay's Week 9 win over the Patriots after fracturing his ring finger and has already been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Vikings. A more precise recovery timeline is expected to be established after Jacobs undergoes surgery on the injured finger Friday, though initial estimates put his likely absence at 2-to-3 weeks on the optimistic side. MarShawn Lloyd, Kaleb Johnson and Pierre Strong are set to lead Green Bay's backfield while Jacobs is sidelined.

injuryReports.name: Trey Smack
injuryReports.returnComment: Per Rob Demovsky of ESPN.com, LaFleur added that he isn't concerned with Smack's mechanics being affected by the kicker's right calf injury based on Smack's performance at Wednesday's practice. If Smack returns to full participation Thursday after being limited Wednesday, that would put him in the clear to face the Vikings on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Evan Williams
injuryReports.returnComment: Brandon Cisse broke up a deep pass from Drake Maye to Kyle Williams early in the second quarter, and Williams was able to make a toe-tapping grab for the takeaway. Williams is up to three interceptions on the year, which ties his career high that he set across 16 regular-season games in 2025. The third-year defensive back is up to 76 tackles (48 solo), including 1.0 sacks, seven pass defenses and one fumble recovery through nine regular-season games.
injuryReports.injury: Williams logged five tackles (four solo) and one interception during the Packers' 45-27 win over the Patriots in Week 9.

injuryReports.name: Xavier McKinney
injuryReports.returnComment: Both of McKinney's interceptions took place in the first half, and the Packers offense capitalized by scoring touchdowns off of each of those two takeaways. It was the second time this season that McKinney logged two picks, and his five interceptions are tied with Amani Hooker for most in the NFL. McKinney is up to 38 tackles (22 solo), including 1.0 sacks, and six pass defenses through nine regular-season games.
injuryReports.injury: McKinney posted four tackles (two solo) and two interceptions during the Packers' 45-27 win over the Patriots in Week 9.

injuryReports.name: Isaiah McDuffie
injuryReports.returnComment: McDuffie's first tackle of the game was a nine-yard sack on Drake Maye early in the first quarter, which led to the Patriots punting the ball away on the next play. McDuffie also recovered the fumble he forced late in the third quarter, which the Packers offense turned into a 37-yard touchdown pass from Jordan Love to Christian Watson one play later. McDuffie has racked up double-digit stops in three consecutive games, and he's been the starting inside linebacker in each of those contests due to the absence of Zaire Franklin (shin). McDuffie should hang onto his starting role against the Vikings on Sunday assuming Franklin is ruled out for that game.
injuryReports.injury: McDuffie registered 10 tackles (five solo), including 1.0 sacks, one forced fumble and one fumble recovery during the Packers' 45-27 win over the Patriots in Week 9.

injuryReports.name: Ty'Ron Hopper
injuryReports.returnComment: Hopper picked up a chest injury during the first quarter of the Packers' win against the Patriots in Week 9 and did not return. The good news for the third-year pro is that he was cleared to practice in a limited fashion Wednesday. If Hopper can upgrade his participation over the next two days, then he would likely avoid an injury designation for Sunday's NFC North showdown against the Vikings.

injuryReports.name: Javon Bullard
injuryReports.returnComment: Bullard may have tweaked his ankle during the Packers' win over the Patriots in Week 9, when he logged three tackles (two solo). He'll have two more chances to return to practice ahead of Sunday's game against the Vikings, but if he cannot play in that contest, then Kamal Hadden, Carrington Valentine and Benjamin St-Juste would all be in line for more defensive snaps in the secondary.

injuryReports.name: Zaire Franklin
injuryReports.returnComment: doubtful

injuryReports.name: Lukas Van Ness
injuryReports.returnComment: The Packers hosted a jog-through practice Wednesday, but Van Ness was a spectator for that session due to a back injury that he may have picked up during the Packers' Week 9 win over the Patriots, when he logged one solo tackle. He'll have two more opportunities to practice in at least a limited capacity ahead of Sunday's NFC North tilt against Minnesota.

injuryReports.name: Bo Melton
injuryReports.returnComment: Melton was removed from this past Sunday's game against the Patriots to be evaluated for a possible concussion. His ability to practice in full Wednesday is an encouraging sign for his availability for Week 10 against the Vikings on Nov. 15. Melton has five catches (on 10 targets) for 34 yards and 372 yards on 14 kickoffs through nine regular-season games, although he has not recorded a reception since Week 7 against the Lions.

injuryReports.name: Skyy Moore
injuryReports.returnComment: Moore was a limited participant in Wednesday's jog-through practice, which was his first on-field action since being placed on injured reserve in mid-October due to an ankle injury. He's mostly operated as a returner on kickoffs and punts this season, but his return would also give the Packers some extra depth at wide receiver.

injuryReports.name: Chris Brooks
injuryReports.returnComment: Brooks continues to work his way back from an ankle injury that caused him to land on injured reserve in early October. He would likely need to log consecutive full practices before being activated from IR. The Packers face the Vikings on Sunday, and Green Bay is expected to be without Josh Jacobs for two to three weeks due to a broken right ring finger, per Ian Rapoport of NFL Network.

injuryReports.name: Kevin Zeitler
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable

injuryReports.name: Aaron Banks
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable

injuryReports.name: Micah Parsons
injuryReports.returnComment: Prior to Wednesday's session, head coach Matt LaFleur told Ryan Wood of USA Today that Parsons wasn't slated to participate Wednesday due to an illness, but he instead did enough to avoid a DNP listing. On top of that, Parsons is expected to return to team drills later this week, so it'll be interesting to see if he goes down as a full participant Thursday and/or Friday. The Packers are exactly one week into a 21-day window in which to evaluate Parsons and activate him from IR, so the team likely will continue to exercise caution with his return to action.

injuryReports.name: Savion Williams
injuryReports.returnComment: It's a new injury for Williams, who previously missed a chunk of the season with an ankle injury. He's been running as the Packers' clear third receiver behind Matthew Golden and Christian Watson over the last few weeks. If Williams is unable to play against Minnesota on Sunday, Bo Melton and J. Michael Sturdivant could see an uptick in snaps, though Skyy Moore (ankle) had his 21-day practice window opened and could also be an option.

injuryReports.name: MarShawn Lloyd
injuryReports.returnComment: The running back appears ready to return to the lineup for Sunday's game against the Vikings after missing Week 9 against New England. With Josh Jacobs (finger) set to miss some time, Lloyd figures to be part of the backfield mix, joining Kaleb Johnson and Pierre Strong.
injuryReports.injury: Lloyd (knee) is not listed on the Packers' injury report Wednesday.

injuryReports.name: Jonnu Smith
injuryReports.returnComment: Jordan Love threw for a massive 372 yards in the victory, but Smith wasn't targeted on any of the quarterback's 29 passes. That's been par for the course this season -- Smith has drawn one or zero targets in five straight appearances. The veteran tight end has had some productive offensive seasons in his career, but it appears Smith isn't going to be a big part of the Packers' passing-game plans this year.
injuryReports.injury: Smith didn't log a target or touch in a 45-27 win over the Patriots on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Pierre Strong Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: With Josh Jacobs (finger) knocked out of the game in the first quarter and set to miss several weeks, Strong figures to see his role expand in Green Bay's backfield, though MarShawn Lloyd, Kaleb Johnson and even Chris Brooks (ankle) are likely to also see snaps in the coming weeks. Strong is not a recommended fantasy target in 12-team leagues.
injuryReports.injury: Strong rushed eight times for 22 yards in Sunday's 45-27 win over the Patriots. He added two catches for 11 yards on two targets.

injuryReports.name: Kaleb Johnson
injuryReports.returnComment: After being a healthy inactive for the Packers' previous two games, Johnson suited up for Sunday's tilt with the Patriots while Lloyd was inactive. With Jacobs leaving the contest late in the first quarter after fracturing his right ring finger, Johnson was thrust into action and delivered the Packers' best rushing performance of the season, finishing with 14 carries for 68 yards and a touchdown in the 45-27 win. Head coach Matt LaFleur relayed Monday that Jacobs will need surgery and could land on injured reserve, and while Lloyd could have a chance at returning to action Week 10, the Packers likely came away encouraged enough by Johnson's showing in Foxborough to give him another turn as their lead option on the ground. Johnson isn't likely to earn much passing-down work, however, as Lloyd, Pierre Strong and Chris Brooks (ankle) -- who could return from IR this week -- are all more capable options in that phase.
injuryReports.injury: Johnson could serve as the Packers' lead option on the ground in Sunday's game against the Vikings with Josh Jacobs (finger) expected to miss multiple weeks and with the status of MarShawn Lloyd (knee) uncertain, Matt Schneidman of The Athletic reports.

injuryReports.name: Josh Whyle
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable

injuryReports.name: Sean Rhyan
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable

injuryReports.name: Travis Glover
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable

injuryReports.name: Tucker Kraft
injuryReports.returnComment: The athletic tight end didn't get in on any of the fun on a day when Jordan Love threw for 372 yards and three touchdowns. Kraft's stat line set (receptions, receiving yards) or tied (targets) season lows, while his work on the ground included a pair of season-high figures. Nevertheless, it was an utterly forgettable showing for Kraft, who'll look to atone in a Week 10 home divisional clash against the Vikings next Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Kraft brought in one of three targets for one yard and rushed twice for eight yards in the Packers' 45-27 win over the Patriots on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Woody Marks
injuryReports.returnComment: After being deemed a limited participant Wednesday, Marks' apparent absence a day later is noteworthy, though it's possible it's maintenance-related. Thursday's upcoming injury report will provide added context on that front, as well as the participation level of fellow RB David Montgomery (groin), who was on the field Thursday.

injuryReports.name: David Montgomery
injuryReports.returnComment: The report adds that coach DeMeco Ryans said that the Texans are pleased with the progress of the running back, who last played in Week 5. The team's upcoming injury report is slated to reveal if Montgomery, who logged a 'DNP' on Wednesday, is officially credited with some level of participation a day later.  Per Wilson, at this stage whether Montgomery will play this weekend against the Browns is still up in the air

injuryReports.name: Will Anderson Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: Anderson had another strong outing, recording two of the team's eight sacks during the victory. The 25-year-old is on pace to have the most productive season of his career, compiling 35 tackles (19 solo), including 9.5 sacks, a forced fumble and a fumble recovery across eight games played.
injuryReports.injury: Anderson logged two tackles (two solo), including 2.0 sacks, during Houston's win over the Chargers on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Jaylin Smith
injuryReports.returnComment: Smith landed on injured reserve in early October due to a hamstring injury. He's progressed enough in his recovery to return to practice and was a limited participant in Wednesday's session. Smith would need to be activated from IR in order to be available for Sunday's game against the Browns.

injuryReports.name: Jake Hummel
injuryReports.returnComment: Hummel was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice, and it was encouraging to see him back on the field after recovering from groin surgery. The Texans face the Browns on Sunday, but Hummel would need to be activated from IR in order to be available for that contest.

injuryReports.name: Azeez Al-Shaair
injuryReports.returnComment: Al-Shaair was working through a groin issue during Week 9 prep but was cleared to play against the Chargers on Sunday, when he logged 10 tackles (four solo) and one pass defense in a 44-22 win for the Texans. He'll have two more chances to increase his practice participation and avoid an injury designation for Week 10 against the Browns on Nov. 15.

injuryReports.name: Brevin Jordan
injuryReports.returnComment: Jordan has dealt with knee and foot injuries this season and has played pretty sparingly behind Dalton Schultz, Foster Moreau and Cade Stover for much of the campaign. Jordan has logged just 29 offensive snaps across nine appearances.

injuryReports.name: Marvin Harrison Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: It's a new injury for the Texans' newest wideout, who has produced just six catches for 60 yards and a touchdown on 11 targets through three games with Houston. Harrison ran just 14 routes on 40 dropbacks last Sunday against the Chargers, tying him with Kayshon Boutte for fourth among Texans wideouts. Xavier Hutchinson and Tank Dell appear to have emerged as the Nos. 2 and 3 receivers behind Nico Collins.

injuryReports.name: Keylan Rutledge
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable

injuryReports.name: Wyatt Teller
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable

injuryReports.name: Tank Dell
injuryReports.returnComment: Dell operated as the Texans' third receiver for much of last Sunday's 44-22 win over the Chargers, running 22 routes on C.J. Stroud's 38 dropbacks. In just his second game since Week 16 of the 2024 campaign, Dell turned nine targets into five catches for 104 yards and a touchdown against Los Angeles. He's become a legitimate name to add in fantasy football ahead of Sunday's Week 10 date with the Browns.

injuryReports.name: Davis Mills
injuryReports.returnComment: Since the Texans had built their lead to 19 with less than five minutes remaining in the fourth quarter, head coach DeMeco Ryans opted to pull starting quarterback C.J. Stroud from the game and handed the offense over to Mills. In what marked his first playing time of the season, Mills directed two possessions. He led the Texans to a field goal with 2:20 remaining, then knelt twice to run out the clock when Houston got the ball back with 1:07 left. With Stroud enjoying a bounce-back campaign, Mills' opportunities will likely be limited to garbage-time situations if Stroud stays healthy.
injuryReports.injury: Mills completed one of two pass attempts for seven yards and lost two yards on two carries in Sunday's 44-22 win over the Chargers.

injuryReports.name: Cade Stover
injuryReports.returnComment: Week 9 marked the first time all season that Stover sat out, with the Texans opting to keep their other four tight ends (Dalton Schultz, Foster Moreau, Brevin Jordan and Marlin Klein) active ahead of him. Through the Texans' first seven games, Stover had played less than half of the offensive snaps in each contest and recorded three receptions for 17 yards on five targets while rushing three times for five yards.
injuryReports.injury: Stover was a healthy inactive for Sunday's 44-22 win over the Chargers.

injuryReports.name: Foster Moreau
injuryReports.returnComment: For the second straight week, Moreau didn't make a mark in the box score. He did technically draw a target (which he didn't catch), but it was wiped out by an accepted defensive penalty. Moreau hasn't had more than two catches in any game this season and has finished with fewer than 10 yards in every contest since Week 3, so he's not a viable fantasy play in virtually any format right now.
injuryReports.injury: Moreau didn't log any targets or touches Sunday in a 44-22 win against the Chargers.

injuryReports.name: Dare Ogunbowale
injuryReports.returnComment: Ogunbowale continued to play a minor role in Houston's offense with just eight offensive snaps. He did, however, record his first touch of the campaign with a three-yard reception in the third quarter. Ogunbowale hasn't been asked to do much despite David Montgomery (groin) being sidelined since Week 5, and with Montgomery potentially getting close to a return, Ogunbowale's role on game days may soon disappear altogether.
injuryReports.injury: Ogunbowale caught his only target for a three-yard gain Sunday in a 44-22 win over the Chargers.

injuryReports.name: Reed Blankenship
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable

injuryReports.name: Ka'imi Fairbairn
injuryReports.returnComment: Fairbairn was able to convert multiple field-goal attempts for the fifth straight game. The kicker made a 56-yarder in the first quarter before later adding makes from 31 and 41 yards in the fourth quarter. On the season, Fairbairn has gone 18-for-19 on field-goal tries, including 7-for-8 from 50-plus yards, over eight contests so far.
injuryReports.injury: Fairbairn went 3-for-3 on field-goal tries and made all five of his PATs during Sunday's 44-22 win over the Chargers.

injuryReports.name: Dalton Schultz
injuryReports.returnComment: Not counting his 12-140-0 receiving explosion in Week 2 when Nico Collins was out with a hamstring injury, Schultz has mustered 23 grabs for 244 yards and no touchdowns across his seven other appearances. He's failed to reach 50 receiving yards in any of those contests and is merely a TE2 in fantasy.
injuryReports.injury: Schultz caught two of four targets for 42 yards in Sunday's 44-22 win over the Chargers.

injuryReports.name: Kayshon Boutte
injuryReports.returnComment: Boutte entered Week 9 action with a cumulative 15-194-0 line on 23 targets through seven appearances this season, so Sunday's performance was a true outburst. It didn't hurt that Boutte and his teammates were facing the only winless team in the NFL, but QB C.J. Stroud took full advantage of the opportunity, including Boutte (twice) among his five TD tosses. Ultimately, the Texans' receiving corps has a clear No. 1 in WR Nico Collins, who is the best bet among the group to produce most weeks.
injuryReports.injury: Boutte erupted for four catches (on five targets) for 125 yards and two touchdowns during Sunday's 44-22 road win against the Chargers.

injuryReports.name: Xavier Hutchinson
injuryReports.returnComment: Hutchinson finished tied with Kayshon Boutte for second on the team in targets behind fellow wideout Tank Dell (nine). Hutchinson was able to reach paydirt for the second straight contest, reeling in a 17-yard touchdown pass from C.J. Stroud for the team's first score of the day in the first quarter. There are many mouths to feed in Houston's passing attack, so Hutchinson will remain a volatile fantasy option ahead of the team's Week 10 matchup with the Browns.
injuryReports.injury: Hutchinson caught three of five targets for 29 yards and a touchdown and  added a 28-yard kick return during Sunday's 44-22 win against the Chargers.

injuryReports.name: Nico Collins
injuryReports.returnComment: Collins was one of four Texans to reach the end zone via a pass from QB C.J. Stroud, who tossed five TDs in all. It marked Collins' first touchdown since Week 4, when he struck twice against the Cowboys, but overall his output from week to week this season has been a bit inconsistent, as he sits on a 28-384-4 line on 39 targets through his six appearances. He'll seek better results next Sunday in Cleveland.
injuryReports.injury: Collins corralled all four of his targets for 55 yards and one touchdown during Sunday's 44-22 victory at the Chargers.

injuryReports.name: C.J. Stroud
injuryReports.returnComment: Stroud matched a career high with his five TD strikes, which went to Xavier Hutchinson (17 yards), Tank Dell (63), Kayshon Boutte (12 and 63) and Nico Collins (13). Moreover, Stroud's 384 passing yards matched the second most in a game in his career. He's now thrown for multiple touchdowns in four of the last five games, a stretch in which he's accounted for a remarkable 1,457 yards through the air and a 13:2 TD:INT. Stroud will attempt to keep things rolling next Sunday, when the Texans visit the Browns.
injuryReports.injury: Stroud completed 21 of 35 passes for 384 yards, five touchdowns and one interception and recorded two carries for 20 yards during Sunday's 44-22 win at the Chargers.

injuryReports.name: CJ Allen
injuryReports.returnComment: With Akeem Davis-Gaither (knee) out versus Dallas, Allen played all 79 defensive snaps for Indy, marking the first time the second-round rookie has played 100 percent of the defensive snaps in a game. He's started back-to-back contests and is up to 25 tackles (nine solo), including 1.0 sacks, and the one pass breakup across six appearances this season.
injuryReports.injury: Allen recorded 10 tackles (three solo) and a pass breakup in Sunday's 27-23 loss to the Cowboys.

injuryReports.name: Bryce Boettcher
injuryReports.returnComment: With Akeem Davis-Gaither (knee) inactive against Dallas, Boettcher saw a spike in playing time alongside CJ Allen at linebacker for the Colts. The fourth-round rookie Boettcher played a season-high 73 percent of the defensive snaps and recorded his first career game with double-digit tackles.
injuryReports.injury: Boettcher recorded 12 tackles (four solo) in Sunday's 27-23 loss to the Cowboys.

injuryReports.name: Hunter Wohler
injuryReports.returnComment: With A.J. Haulcy (ankle) inactive, Wohler made the spot start alongside Cam Bynum at safety for the Colts. Wohler played 98 percent of the defensive snaps against Dallas, easily a new career-high playing-time clip for the second-year safety after he missed his entire rookie season with a foot injury. Once Haulcy returns, Wohler will likely return to a reserve and special-teams role.
injuryReports.injury: Wohler recorded 16 tackles (six solo) in Sunday's 27-23 loss to the Cowboys.

injuryReports.name: A.J. Haulcy
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable

injuryReports.name: Akeem Davis-Gaither
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable

injuryReports.name: Mo Alie-Cox
injuryReports.returnComment: The veteran blocking tight end was injured in last Sunday's loss to the Cowboys. If he can't play Sunday against Miami, Will Mallory, Drew Ogletree and Pharaoh Brown would be next in line for snaps at tight end behind Tyler Warren.

injuryReports.name: Justin Walley
injuryReports.returnComment: After being injured in Week 7, Walley has missed the past two games but appears ready to return to the lineup Sunday against the Dolphins. He's spent most of his time covering the slot for the Colts this season, recording 35 tackles (23 solo), including 1.0 sacks, and three pass breakups across seven appearances.
injuryReports.injury: Walley (knee) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice.

injuryReports.name: Tyler Warren
injuryReports.returnComment: The trade deadline went as well as possible for Warren's fantasy value, considering the Colts moved their top wide receivers but avoided an all-out purge. The only problem is that Warren is already averaging 7.6 targets per game (fourth among TEs) and producing just 39.3 receiving yards per game and 7.2 yards per catch. Efficiency has been the issue, not volume, and the Colts will likely lean on their running game after declining to trade RB Jonathan Taylor. Improved play from Warren and QB Daniel Jones would probably matter more than another increase in target share.
injuryReports.injury: Warren may see more targets after the Colts traded wideouts Josh Downs and Keenan Allen on Tuesday, Chris Bumbaca of ColtsWire reports.

injuryReports.name: Deion Burks
injuryReports.returnComment: A rookie seventh-round pick with 4.30 speed, Burks has caught six of nine targets for 60 yards across 49 routes (18.3 percent target rate, 1.22 yards per route). He won't necessarily see a lot of targets in an offense that runs through the RBs and TEs, but Burks should at least get far more playing time in the second half of the season, if only because the Colts' other wideouts are veterans with minimal history of production. Laquon Treadwell and Ashton Dulin are the other favorites for regular playing time, and Nick Westbrook-Ikhine is also on the roster.
injuryReports.injury: Colts coach Shane Steichen said Wednesday that Burks and Anthony Gould will step into larger roles after the team traded Keenan Allen and Josh Downs, Stephen Holder of ESPN.com reports.

injuryReports.name: Arden Key
injuryReports.returnComment: Key hasn't played since sustaining a hamstring injury in Week 4 against the Commanders. Now, after five weeks, the 30-year-old may begin practicing. He will likely need to string together multiple positive practices for a chance to play in Week 10.

injuryReports.name: Alec Pierce
injuryReports.returnComment: "We'll see. Like I said last week, he's still in that rehab process, and I'm not going to put a timetable on return," Steichen noted of the wideout, who's been on IR since Sept. 26. At 2-7, the Colts were sellers ahead of the NFL's trade deadline, so the team presumably has no reason rush Pierce back. With Keenan Allen and Josh Downs no longer in the mix, Indy's healthy WRs for now are Ashton Dulin, Laquon Treadwell, Anthony Gould, Deion Burks and Nick Westbrook-Ikhine.

injuryReports.name: Ashton Dulin
injuryReports.returnComment: Steichen also mentioned Deion Burks and Nick Westbrook-Ikhine as other candidates to fill in at the outside receiver spot opposite Laquon Treadwell, while noting that Anthony Gould will serve as the Colts' starting slot receiver after the team also traded Josh Downs to the Chiefs on Tuesday. With Alec Pierce's (heel) return from injured reserve seemingly not imminent, Dulin could have a prime opportunity to see extended snaps over the next few weeks, provided he can hold off the likes of Burks and Westbrook-Ikhine for playing time. Dulin already made a bit of a splash in the Colts' Week 9 loss to the Cowboys, connecting with Daniel Jones on a 55-yard touchdown reception while also carrying once for a three-yard gain.
injuryReports.injury: Head coach Shane Steichen said that Dulin will be one of the Colts receivers tasked with absorbing the snaps vacated by Keenan Allen, who was traded to the 49ers on Tuesday, Jake Arthur of Roundtable.io reports.

injuryReports.name: Anthony Gould
injuryReports.returnComment: With both Downs and Keenan Allen having been dealt by the Colts on Tuesday, the team will be operating with a re-shaped WR corps going forward. According to the Colts' latest unofficial depth chart, Gould is indeed listed a first-teamer along with Ashton Dulin and Laquon Treadwell. Also expected to have additional opportunities in the coming weeks will be 2026 seventh-rounder Deion Burks, with veteran pass catcher Nick Westbrook-Ikhine in the mix as well after being signed off the practice squad. Though a wait-and-see approach is in order in term's of Gould's fantasy lineup viability, his production beginning this weekend versus Miami is worth tracking by those in deeper PPR formats.
injuryReports.injury: Colts coach Shane Steichen said Wednesday that Gould is in line to step into the slot role previously held by Josh Downs, Stephen Holder of ESPN.com reports.

injuryReports.name: Luke Rhodes
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable

injuryReports.name: Laquon Treadwell
injuryReports.returnComment: Since drawing a season-high eight targets in a Week 5 loss to the Steelers, Treadwell has barely surpassed that total over the past four games combined. Despite handling snap shares north of 70 percent in each of those contests, Treadwell has mustered a 5-58-0 receiving line on 10 targets during that stretch. The Colts will have more target volume up for grabs after trading Keenan Allen to the 49ers and Josh Downs to Kansas City on Tuesday, and though Treadwell could be one of the beneficiaries, he still looks to be a low-upside fantasy option.
injuryReports.injury: Treadwell logged 52 of the Colts' 64 snaps and was held without a reception on one target in Sunday's 27-23 loss to the Cowboys.

injuryReports.name: Nick Westbrook-Ikhine
injuryReports.returnComment: Indianapolis will turn to Westbrook-Ikhine to fill the 53-man roster spot vacated by Keenan Allen, who was traded to the 49ers on Tuesday. Westbrook-Ikhine had previously been elevated from the Colts' practice squad for three straight games between Weeks 3 and 5 and failed to corral his lone target while logging 18 total snaps on offense. He'll fill a depth role in the Colts' receiving corps and could end up providing most of his value on the team's coverage and return units on special teams.
injuryReports.injury: The Colts signed Westbrook-Ikhine off their practice squad Tuesday.

injuryReports.name: Jonathan Taylor
injuryReports.returnComment: In order to move Taylor, Indianapolis was reportedly seeking a blockbuster trade package on par with what Carolina received in exchange for Christian McCaffrey back in 2022, but Pelissero relays that inquiring teams weren't willing to meet that price tag. As a result, Taylor -- who is under contract through 2028 -- will stick around in Indianapolis through the remainder of the campaign, though it's possible that the Colts entertain trade offers for the 27-year-old running back again during the offseason.
injuryReports.injury: The Colts informed Taylor that he won't be traded before Tuesday's deadline, Tom Pelissero of Netflix reports.

injuryReports.name: Jalen Travis
injuryReports.returnComment: doubtful

injuryReports.name: DJ Giddens
injuryReports.returnComment: Giddens didn't see any action after turning six carries into 43 yards in Week 8 against the Jaguars. With Jonathan Taylor potentially set to be traded before Tuesday's NFL trade deadline, Giddens would stand to operate as the team's No. 2 option in the backfield behind rookie Seth McGowan if Taylor departs.
injuryReports.injury: Giddens was active but didn't play in Sunday's 27-23 loss to the Cowboys.

injuryReports.name: Spencer Shrader
injuryReports.returnComment: Shrader entered Week 9 having made just three field goals over the team's last three games, but he got back on track Sunday. The kicker made a 47-yard attempt in the third quarter before adding makes from 59 and 50 yards in the final quarter. Shrader has now converted multiple field-goal attempts in six contests this year, and he's gone 22-for-24 on field-goal tries, including 8-for-9 from 50-plus yards, over nine contests so far during the 2026 campaign.
injuryReports.injury: Shrader went 3-for-3 on field-goal tries and made both of his PATs during Sunday's 27-23 loss to the Cowboys.

injuryReports.name: Seth McGowan
injuryReports.returnComment: McGowan recorded his first NFL touchdown on a two-yard run in the first quarter, perhaps a harbinger of a larger role as early as next Sunday's Week 10 matchup against the Dolphins. McGowan came just a rush yard short of equaling his career-best tally in that category, and if Jonathan Taylor is indeed moved off the roster by Tuesday's trade deadline, the former would be in line to serve as the lead back moving forward.
injuryReports.injury: McGowan rushed six times for 45 yards and a touchdown and brought in his only target for minus-3 yards in the Colts' 27-23 loss to the Cowboys on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Bhayshul Tuten
injuryReports.returnComment: Tuten was deemed a non-participant in practice Wednesday, but his presence on the field a day later suggests that he could advance to limited participation Thursday. In any case, the Jaguars' next practice report will clarify that, as well as how much work fellow RB Chris Rodriguez (hand) got in.

injuryReports.name: B.J. Green II
injuryReports.returnComment: Green landed on injured reserve in mid-September after suffering an elbow injury in Week 1 against the Browns. The Jaguars now have 21 days to activate Green from injured reserve, otherwise the Colorado product would be sidelined for the rest of the 2026 season.

injuryReports.name: Travon Walker
injuryReports.returnComment: Walker played through a questionable tag last Thursday night against the Ravens and saw his normal allotment of snaps, playing 68 percent of the downs on defense. The 25-year-old has produced 21 tackles (nine solo), including 3.0 sacks, eight QB hits and one pass breakup across eight games this season.

injuryReports.name: Antonio Johnson
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable

injuryReports.name: Branson Combs
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable

injuryReports.name: Robert Hainsey
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable

injuryReports.name: Ezra Cleveland
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable

injuryReports.name: Chris Rodriguez Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: While Rodriguez fit some work in on Wednesday, fellow RB Bhayshul Tuten (ankle/foot) was listed as a DNP by the Jaguars. The duo's status is thus worth monitoring closely in the coming days, but if Tuten ends up limited or out this weekend, Rodriguez -- if available -- and Ameer Abdullah would be next up for the team's backfield touches Sunday against the Titans.

injuryReports.name: Jakobi Meyers
injuryReports.returnComment: Meyers was listed with hamstring and ankle injuries last week before playing 68 percent of Jacksonville's offensive snaps and catching four passes for 65 yards in a Thursday blowout at Baltimore. It's unclear if the ankle has worsened or if Wednesday's absence is just a matter of caution/maintenance. Brian Thomas, Josh Cameron and Travis Hunter would all be candidates for additional WR snaps if Meyers were to miss time.

injuryReports.name: Brian Thomas Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: After sending out a first-round pick, two second-round picks, a fifth-round pick and a sixth-round pick Monday in separate deals to bring in defenders Jordan Davis, Jessie Bates and Davon Godchaux, the Jaguars likely could have recouped some of that draft capital if they had opted to move Thomas. Instead, Fowler indicates that the Jaguars plan to keep the rest of their roster intact ahead of the deadline, which will result in Thomas sticking around. Rather than operating as the high-volume target earner he was during his banner 2024 rookie campaign, Thomas looks like he'll continue to serve mainly as a vertical threat who frees up opportunities in the short and intermediate areas for other pass catchers. Thomas has drawn three or fewer targets in six straight games, producing a weak 4-37-2 receiving line during that stretch.
injuryReports.injury: The Jaguars have relayed to inquiring teams that they intend to keep Thomas through Tuesday's trade deadline, Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.com reports.

injuryReports.name: Davon Godchaux
injuryReports.returnComment: Godchaux was selected by Miami in the fifth round of the 2017 NFL Draft. Since then, he has appeared in 145 regular-season games for the Dolphins, Patriots and Saints, garnering 487 total tackles (224 solo), 5.5 sacks and three forced fumbles. Godchaux's presence will bolster depth at the defensive tackle position for the Jaguars, especially with DaVon Hamilton (knee) done for the remainder of the 2026 campaign.
injuryReports.injury: The Jaguars acquired Godchaux from the Saints on Monday in exchange for a 2028 sixth-round pick, though the selection could turn into a 2027 sixth-round pick if "conditions are met," Jonathan Jones of The Athletic of The Athletic reports.

injuryReports.name: Foyesade Oluokun
injuryReports.returnComment: Oluokun tied for his team's lead in stops and notched his second sack of the season when he brought down Joe Fagnano early in the second quarter. Oluokun has been a reliable fantasy IDP asset in 2026 with at least seven tackles in six of his eight games so far. He's tallied 58 total stops, including the 2.0 sacks, along with two interceptions and a forced fumble.
injuryReports.injury: Oluokun recorded seven tackles (six solo), including 1.0 sacks, in Thursday's 33-10 victory over Baltimore.

injuryReports.name: Tanner Koziol
injuryReports.returnComment: Koziol was part of a three-tight-end starting unit for Jacksonville alongside Brenton Strange and Nate Boerkircher. Koziol logged the fewest offensive snaps (12) among the trio but matched both in receptions. He entered Thursday with just one catch through five contests, so it's probably not wise to count on him for substantial production moving forward.
injuryReports.injury: Koziol finished Thursday's 33-10 win over Baltimore with two catches for 15 yards on two targets.

injuryReports.name: Nate Boerkircher
injuryReports.returnComment: Boerkircher was tied with Parker Washington for the second-most receiving yards on the team with 61. This game marks the fourth time this season that the rookie has surpassed 30 snaps on offense. Boerkircher has made a name for himself as Jacksonville's No. 2 option at tight end behind Brenton Strange.
injuryReports.injury: Boerkircher hauled in two of three targets for 61 yards in Thursday night's 33-10 win over Baltimore.

injuryReports.name: Josh Cameron
injuryReports.returnComment: Cameron didn't see the ball until the fourth quarter despite playing the third most snaps at wide receiver (25) for the Jaguars on Thursday, behind only Parker Washington (38) and Jakobi Meyers (38). This marks the third game in a row during which the 23-year-old played as the Jaguars' No. 3 option at receiver, but his limited usage keeps him as a low-priority waiver-wire add.
injuryReports.injury: Cameron caught his only target for six yards in Thursday night's 33-10 victory over the Ravens.

injuryReports.name: Ameer Abdullah
injuryReports.returnComment: Abdullah recorded the third-most-offensive snaps in the backfield (seven), behind Chris Rodriguez (25) and Bayshul Tuten (20). Should everyone in the backfield remain healthy, Abdullah will likely see a similar workload for the rest of the season.
injuryReports.injury: Abdullah carried the ball seven times for 30 yards and returned one kickoff for 24 yards in Thursday night's 33-10 win over the Ravens.

injuryReports.name: Brenton Strange
injuryReports.returnComment: The Jaguars keep blowing teams out and aren't being pushed on offense, which is keeping Trevor Lawrence's pass volume low. Strange is still making the most of his few opportunities, totaling four grabs for 77 yards on four targets over the last two weeks, games in which the Jaguars have combined to outscore their opponents 75-17. Strange is a TE1 for fantasy and gets a date with the Titans on Sunday, Nov. 15.
injuryReports.injury: Strange caught both of his targets for 22 yards in Thursday night's 33-10 win over the Ravens.

injuryReports.name: Travis Hunter
injuryReports.returnComment: Hunter played six offensive snaps against Baltimore but turned the ball over on his only touch. After posting a 4-59-1 receiving line against the Texans in London back in Week 6, Hunter has done very little on offense. He needs the Jaguars' opponents to make games closer so the coaching staff feels obligated to utilize Hunter's big-play ability.
injuryReports.injury: Hunter caught his only target for minus-1 yard and lost a fumble in Thursday night's 33-10 win over the Ravens.

injuryReports.name: Cam Little
injuryReports.returnComment: The Jaguars dominated in the victory, but they fell short of the end zone enough times to keep Little busy. He didn't need to fully flex the strength of his leg, as his longest kick was from a modest 47 yards out, but Little extended his run of consecutive successful FG attempts to 10. He's now gone 14-of-16 on field-goal tries this season while converting 25 of 26 point-after attempts.
injuryReports.injury: Little made all four of his field-goal attempts and all three of his extra-point tries in a 33-10 win over Baltimore on Thursday.

injuryReports.name: Trevor Lawrence
injuryReports.returnComment: Lawrence unsurprisingly didn't have a high-volume night, as the Jaguars were progressively able to take control of the game with Joe Fagnano under center for the Ravens. The veteran signal-caller hit Parker Washington on a 50-yard catch-and-run touchdown over the middle just before halftime for his one scoring pass, and Lawrence connected with eight different targets overall on the night. The 2021 first overall pick has now thrown for 1,932 yards with an 18:4 TD:INT and added 79 yards on the ground heading into a Week 10 road matchup against the Titans on Sunday, Nov. 15.
injuryReports.injury: Lawrence completed 16 of 26 passes for 242 yards with a touchdown and no interceptions while rushing once for minus-1 yard in the Jaguars' 33-16 win over the Ravens on Thursday night.

injuryReports.name: Parker Washington
injuryReports.returnComment: Washington led the Jaguars in targets while tying for second in receptions and receiving yards on the night. The fourth-year receiver snapped a two-game touchdown drought, crossing the goal line from 50 yards out on a catch and run over the middle with under a minute remaining in the first half. Washington has eclipsed 60 receiving yards in three of the past four games heading into a Week 10 road matchup against the Titans on Sunday, Nov. 15.
injuryReports.injury: Washington secured two of seven targets for 61 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars' 33-10 win over the Ravens on Thursday night. He also returned one punt for 11 yards.

injuryReports.name: Cam'Ron Silmon-Craig
injuryReports.returnComment: inactive

injuryReports.name: Chris Jones
injuryReports.returnComment: The 32-year-old defensive lineman had gotten off to a slow start to begin the 2026 season, his 11th in the league. Prior to Sunday, he'd recorded just 0.5 sacks across the first seven games, so his 2.0 sacks were his first full ones of the campaign. Jones is now up to 17 tackles (eight solo), including 2.5 sacks, three pass breakups and a fumble recovery on 72 percent of the defensive snaps.
injuryReports.injury: Jones recorded four tackles (two solo), including 2.0 sacks, and a pass breakup in Sunday's 35-12 win over the Jets.

injuryReports.name: George Karlaftis
injuryReports.returnComment: After starting the season without a sack in his first four games, Karlaftis has 4.0 sacks over his last four contests. For the season, the 25-year-old edge rusher is up to 32 tackles (16 solo), including the 4.0 sacks, a career-high nine pass breakups, including his first career interception, and a forced fumble across eight games. He's on pace to shatter his previous career high of 48 tackles, which was set last season.
injuryReports.injury: Karlaftis recorded six tackles (four solo), including 2.0 sacks, and a pass breakup in Sunday's 35-12 win over the Jets.

injuryReports.name: Nick Bolton
injuryReports.returnComment: Bolton doesn't do much in the box scores other than rack up tackles, but he's good at that and now has five double-digit tackles games through eight contests to begin the 2026 campaign. For the season, Bolton is up to 80 tackles (39 solo), two pass breakups and a forced fumble on 99 percent of the Chiefs' defensive snaps.
injuryReports.injury: Bolton recorded 12 tackles (five solo) and a forced fumble in Sunday's 35-12 win over the Jets.

injuryReports.name: Drue Tranquill
injuryReports.returnComment: It was Tranquill's second double-digit tackles game of the season, and both have come over the last three weeks. The veteran linebacker has piled up 66 tackles (33 solo), two pass breakups and one fumble recovery on 88 percent of the defensive snaps across eight games this season.
injuryReports.injury: Tranquill collected 13 tackles (seven solo) in Sunday's 35-12 win over the Jets.

injuryReports.name: Mansoor Delane
injuryReports.returnComment: The first-round rookie cornerback appears set to return to the lineup Sunday against the Falcons after missing the previous two contests. Delane has been dealing with the shoulder issue since initially injuring it during the offseason program. Across five games this season, Delane has 27 tackles (17 solo) and five pass breakups, including an interception.
injuryReports.injury: Delane (shoulder) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice.

injuryReports.name: Patrick Mahomes
injuryReports.returnComment: As were Rashee Rice (knee) as well as Xavier Worthy (hamstring), and with Chiefs having added Josh Downs (who is not on the injury report) via a trade with the Colts, the team heads into Sunday's game against the Falcons with its franchise QB and top three WRs presumably available for Week 10 action. Mahomes clearly endured some elbow discomfort during the Chiefs' Week 9 win over the Jets, but the issue is something he'll continue to play through.
injuryReports.injury: Mahomes (right elbow/knee) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice.

injuryReports.name: Xavier Worthy
injuryReports.returnComment: Worthy was considered day-to-day after exiting Sunday's 35-12 win over the Jets in the fourth quarter. A quick return to full practice participation suggests Worthy will be fine for the upcoming matchup with Atlanta on Sunday, but his target share may decline in the second half of the season after Kansas City traded for WR Josh Downs.
injuryReports.injury: Worthy (hamstring) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice for Kansas City.

injuryReports.name: Harrison Butker
injuryReports.returnComment: On that topic, coach Andy Reid said Wednesday, "I'm gonna stick with Butker this week." While the veteran kicker has held on to the top job through the Chiefs' first eight games, he's had accuracy issues this season, having converted 12 of his 19 field-goal attempts and making 22 of his 23 extra-point tries in that span. Reid's comment about Butker on Wednesday implies that the team's kicking situation is being evaluated on a weekly basis. Justin Tucker is on Kansas City's practice squad, and he remains an option should Reid decide that a switch is in order down the road.
injuryReports.injury: Butker will remain Kansas City's kicker ahead of Sunday's game against the Falcons, Sam McDowell of The Kansas City Star reports.

injuryReports.name: Justin Fields
injuryReports.returnComment: The Chiefs' backup quarterback saw the field for just the second time this season, after he had previously played one snap in a Week 1 win over the Broncos. Due to head coach Andy Reid's reluctance to use starter Patrick Mahomes on quarterback sneaks, Fields subbed into the game for a third-and-1 play in the first quarter. Fields ended up coughing the football, with the Jets making the recovery. The Chiefs went on to build enough of a lead to rest Mahomes for the final possession of the game with just over two minutes left in the fourth quarter, when Fields proceeded to hand the ball off three times before kneeling to run out the clock.
injuryReports.injury: Fields carried twice for minus-one yard and lost a fumble while logging five snaps on offense in Sunday's 35-12 win over the Jets.

injuryReports.name: Jalen Royals
injuryReports.returnComment: Royals ranked fourth among KC wideouts in offensive snaps (21), trailing Xavier Worthy (49), Rashee Rice (38) and Andrew Armstrong (22). Royals matched his season high with two catches, and the 18 receiving yards were his second-most in a game this season. That speaks to the minimal production he's provided thus far, and Royals' role could be further reduced with the Chiefs' acquisition of Josh Downs on Tuesday.
injuryReports.injury: Royals caught both of his targets for 18 yards Sunday in a 35-12 rout of the Jets.

injuryReports.name: Peter Woods
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable

injuryReports.name: Noah Gray
injuryReports.returnComment: Gray was a minor factor in the passing game, with his lone reception gaining 11 yards late in the third quarter. Meanwhile, No. 1 tight end Travis Kelce paced Kansas City with 72 receiving yards on four catches. Gray had a nice two-game run with a combined six catches for 97 yards across Weeks 6 and 7, but since then he's tallied just three receptions for 26 yards and a touchdown across his subsequent two games.
injuryReports.injury: Gray caught his only target for 11 yards Sunday in a 35-12 win against the Jets.

injuryReports.name: Cyrus Allen
injuryReports.returnComment: Allen made the start at wide receiver but ran just 13 routes on Patrick Mahomes' 36 dropbacks against New York. With Xavier Worthy (hamstring) now injured, Allen could have a path to more playing time moving forward, but all three of Rashee Rice, Kenneth Walker and Travis Kelce are well ahead of the rookie wideout for targets.
injuryReports.injury: Allen failed to catch his only target in Sunday's 35-12 win over the Jets.

injuryReports.name: Jaylon Moore
injuryReports.returnComment: Moore suffered an ankle injury in Sunday's win over the Jets. While he hasn't been ruled out for Week 10 versus the Falcons, there's certainly the possibility of an absence. If that's the case, Joshua Ezeudu may fill the void at right tackle.

injuryReports.name: Emmett Johnson
injuryReports.returnComment: The Chiefs held a 28-12 lead by the end of three quarters, which provided the opportunity for head coach Andy Reid to give Kenneth Walker, who scored three total touchdowns, some down time in the latter portion of the contest. Johnson took advantage of his opportunities, recording a six-yard touchdown run with 3:35 remaining. The rookie fifth-round pick's yardage total was a new career high, while his carry tally was his highest since Week 3. Johnson will remain in a modest No. 2 role for a Week 10 road matchup against the Falcons next Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Johnson rushed six times for 34 yards and a touchdown and returned one kickoff for 29 yards in the Chiefs' 35-12 win over the Jets on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Rashee Rice
injuryReports.returnComment: Rice led the Chiefs in targets while finishing as the runner-up in both receptions and receiving yards. The veteran receiver has been busy the last two games while turning 15 targets into a 12-102-1 line, but he has just one catch of 20-plus yards in that span. Rice is averaging a relatively modest 11.7 yards per catch heading into a Week 10 road matchup against the Falcons.
injuryReports.injury: Rice secured five of seven targets for 49 yards in the Chiefs' 35-12 win over the Jets on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Travis Kelce
injuryReports.returnComment: Kelce led the Chiefs in receiving yards and finished second in targets on the afternoon, and his tally in the former category also served as the legendary tight end's second highest of the season. Kelce got there with a big boost from a game-high 38-yard catch, and he'll take a formidable 33-482-2 line into a Week 10 road matchup against the Falcons next Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Kelce brought in four of six targets for 72 yards in the Chiefs' 35-12 win over the Jets on Sunday. He also rushed once for one yard.

injuryReports.name: Kenneth Walker III
injuryReports.returnComment: Walker put together another one of his signature high-efficiency performances on the ground, averaging 5.7 yards per carry in the process. He contributed a seven-yard touchdown reception on the first play of the second quarter, and he struck again as a receiver via a 25-yard scoring grab with just over five minutes remaining in the first half. Walker capped off the highly fantasy-friendly day with his seventh rushing touchdown of the season, a two-yard run in the waning moments of the third quarter. Walker is up to 872 rushing yards, 172 receiving yards and 11 total touchdowns heading into a Week 10 road matchup against the Falcons next Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Walker rushed 18 times for 102 yards and a touchdown and brought in all four targets for 41 yards and two more scores in the Chiefs' 35-12 win over the Jets on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: L'Jarius Sneed
injuryReports.returnComment: Sneed was initially given the questionable tag for Sunday's game against the Broncos. He's been able to play through a lingering knee issue, but his placement on IR indicates that the injury has gotten to the point that an extended absence is warranted for the seventh-year defensive back. Sneed will be required to miss at least four games, so the earliest he can return is Week 12 against the Bills on Thursday, Nov. 26. Jaden Hicks, Jadon Canady, Kristian Fulton and Christian Roland-Wallace are all candidates to see more work in the secondary due to the absences of both Sneed and Mansoor Delane (shoulder) for Sunday's AFC West tilt.

injuryReports.name: Treydan Stukes
injuryReports.returnComment: Stukes jumped in front of a Brock Purdy pass intended for George Kittle midway through the third quarter, although the Raiders' offense gave the ball right back to the 49ers two plays later on a Brock Bowers fumble. It was the second interception of the season for Stukes, who was a second-round selection of the Raiders in the 2026 NFL Draft. The rookie out of Arizona is up to 43 tackles (23 solo) and four pass defenses through the first eight regular-season games of his NFL career.
injuryReports.injury: Stukes registered five tackles (three solo) and an interception during the Raiders' 38-17 loss to the 49ers in Week 9.

injuryReports.name: Jeremy Chinn
injuryReports.returnComment: Chinn finished Week 9 as the Raiders' third-leading tackler behind Nakobe Dean (19) and Quay Walker (11). Dean has logged at least seven stops in five consecutive outings, and he has accumulated 66 tackles (44 solo), including 1.0 sacks, two pass defenses (including one interception), two forced fumbles and two fumble recoveries over nine regular-season games.
injuryReports.injury: Chinn recorded nine tackles (six solo) during the Raiders' 38-17 loss to the 49ers in Week 9.

injuryReports.name: Quay Walker
injuryReports.returnComment: It was the second time in three games that Walker finished with double-digit stops, and he finished second on the Raiders in tackles behind Nakobe Dean (19). Walker is on track for his fifth consecutive 100-plus tackle campaign and is up to 72 stops (28 solo), including 2.0 sacks, and one fumble recovery through nine regular-season games.
injuryReports.injury: Walker posted 11 tackles (three solo) during the Raiders' 38-17 loss to the 49ers in Week 9.

injuryReports.name: Nakobe Dean
injuryReports.returnComment: Dean played every defensive snap and was all over the field in Week 9, finishing with a career-best 19 total tackles. He's logged at least 12 tackles in six of his last seven outings, and through nine regular-season games he has accumulated 98 total tackles, which is second-most in the NFL behind Alex Singleton (107).
injuryReports.injury: Dean logged 19 tackles (seven solo) during the Raiders' 38-17 loss to the 49ers in Week 9.

injuryReports.name: Trey Zuhn III
injuryReports.returnComment: Zuhn entered the league's concussion protocol during the Raiders' Week 9 loss to the 49ers. He'll need to clear protocol in order to play against the Seahawks on Sunday, otherwise Caleb Rogers would likely serve as the Raiders' starting right guard.

injuryReports.name: Folorunso Fatukasi
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable

injuryReports.name: Aidan O'Connell
injuryReports.returnComment: O'Connell is set to back up rookie Mendoza, who replaced recently traded Kirk Cousins as the starting quarterback. O'Connell has been with Las Vegas since the team drafted him in the fourth round of the 2023 NFL Draft. The 28-year-old last appeared in a regular-season game in 2025, completing 10 of 22 attempts for 102 yards.
injuryReports.injury: O'Connell moves to QB No. 2 on the depth chart behind Fernando Mendoza, Sam Warren of The Athletic reports.

injuryReports.name: Jack Bech
injuryReports.returnComment: Bech logged a 34 percent offensive snap share, third-highest among Raiders wideouts behind Jalen Nailor (74 percent) and Tre Tucker (64 percent). Though he seems fairly secure in the No. 3 wideout role, Bech hasn't done much this season, producing no more than three catches or 25 yards in any of his five games to date.
injuryReports.injury: Bech caught one of two targets for nine yards Sunday in a loss to the 49ers.

injuryReports.name: Fernando Mendoza
injuryReports.returnComment: The No. 1 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft has opened his professional career on the bench, with his lone action to date coming during garbage time of a blowout loss to the Patriots in Week 5, when he completed six of eight pass attempts for 48 yards. However, with the 4-5 Raiders shipping out Cousins for a 2027 third-round pick, the 23-year-old Mendoza will now be thrust into his first extended NFL playing time and will face a pair of tough defenses off the bat, as he'll follow up the matchup against the Seahawks with a road game in Denver in Week 11. Mendoza had underwhelming numbers over his three preseason appearances, but he's reportedly been "tearing it up in practice" during the regular season and has given the Raiders optimism that he's ready to lead the offense, per Matt Zenitz of CBSSports.com.
injuryReports.injury: Mendoza will take over as the Raiders' new starting quarterback beginning with Sunday's game versus the Seahawks after Las Vegas traded Kirk Cousins to Minnesota on Tuesday, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.

injuryReports.name: Thomas Booker IV
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable

injuryReports.name: Matt Gay
injuryReports.returnComment: Gay's lone field goal came from 50 yards in the second quarter, and he now has made three of his four kicks from 50 yards or longer on the season. The 32-year-old is 19-for-21 on field-goal attempts and a perfect 21-for-21 on extra-point tries across nine appearances.
injuryReports.injury: Gay converted his only field-goal attempt and both of his extra-point tries during Las Vegas' loss to the 49ers on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Jalen Nailor
injuryReports.returnComment: Nailor was a non-factor on offense in Week 9, failing to reach double-digit receiving yards for the fourth time this season. The wide receiver has had a hard time getting into a groove in his first season with Las Vegas, catching 14 of 28 targets for 122 yards and a touchdown over eight contests so far.
injuryReports.injury: Nailor caught two of four targets for nine yards during Sunday's 38-17 loss to the 49ers.

injuryReports.name: Michael Mayer
injuryReports.returnComment: The tight end was inches and a couple breaks away from having a much bigger afternoon, as he lost a fumble just before crossing the goal line on what would have been a 25-yard touchdown. He then had another score called back on a penalty in the second half. Mayer has alternated big games with down ones this season, and he'll try to rebound next Sunday in a tough spot against the Seahawks' strong defense.
injuryReports.injury: Mayer caught all three of his targets for 37 yards in Sunday's 38-17 loss to the 49ers.

injuryReports.name: Mike Washington Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: The rookie running back wasn't targeted in the passing game. One week after getting a trial run as the Raiders' clear lead back, a game in which he produced 83 yards on 25 carries, Washington was out-snapped 32 to 17 by Ashton Jeanty against San Francisco. He's averaging just 3.9 yards per carry on 71 totes this season and has just three receptions, though it's worth noting that Jeanty has been even less efficient as a ball carrier with only 3.1 YPC. Washington is a fantasy bench stash, but the Raiders' rushing attack seems broken as a whole.
injuryReports.injury: Washington turned six carries into minus-three yards in Sunday's 38-17 loss to the 49ers.

injuryReports.name: Tre Tucker
injuryReports.returnComment: Tucker finished tied for the team lead in targets with tight end Brock Bowers, garnering at least five targets for the fifth time in the team's last six contests. The wide receiver rebounded well after being blanked in Week 8 versus the Jets, securing four or more receptions for the seventh time this season. Tucker has now reeled in 33 of 56 targets for 529 yards and four touchdowns over the Raiders' first nine games during the 2026 campaign.
injuryReports.injury: Tucker caught four of eight targets for 55 yards during Sunday's 38-17 loss to the 49ers.

injuryReports.name: Ashton Jeanty
injuryReports.returnComment: The Raiders largely abandoned the run after going down 14-0 early, but Jeanty was more effective with his six carries than Mike Washington, who rushed six times for minus-3 yards and finished without a target. Sunday's even distribution in carries was a positive development for Jeanty, who had just two rushing attempts to Washington's 25 in the Week 8 win over the Jets. Jeanty still has more receiving yards (371) than rushing yards (362) and is averaging just 3.2 yards per carry heading into a difficult Week 10 matchup against Seattle's elite front seven.
injuryReports.injury: Jeanty rushed six times for 25 yards while catching five of seven targets for minus-5 yards in Sunday's 38-17 loss to the 49ers.

injuryReports.name: Brock Bowers
injuryReports.returnComment: Bowers had a 21-yard touchdown reception in the third quarter and came one yard short of scoring again on a 33-yard catch on a fourth-quarter drive that ended with a Kirk Cousins interception in the end zone. The star TE has reached 70 receiving yards in all seven of his appearances this season and is up to six touchdowns. Bowers came five receiving yards shy of his season high and continues to roll, even as the 4-5 Raiders drop out of contention in the AFC. He'll likely face more resistance in Week 10 against the Seahawks, who just held Cardinals TE Trey McBride to 54 yards.
injuryReports.injury: Bowers caught seven of eight targets for 111 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 38-17 loss to the 49ers. He also rushed once for two yards and lost a fumble.

injuryReports.name: Darien Porter
injuryReports.returnComment: Porter suffered a groin injury last Sunday against the Jets and logged a DNP/LP/FP practice progression this week. He was questionable to suit up entering Sunday but will ultimately be able to give it a go. Porter ranks second on the Raiders with five defensed passes on the season.
injuryReports.injury: Porter (groin) is active for Sunday's Week 9 battle against the 49ers.

injuryReports.name: Cody White
injuryReports.returnComment: White was released by the team Tuesday to make room for Carter Runyon (foot), who was activated off injured reserve. With Runyon now waived and potentially joining the Raiders' practice squad, White was re-signed. To date, the 27-year-old has had the best season of his career, amassing eight catches (19 targets) for 112 yards and three touchdowns.
injuryReports.injury: White was signed by the Raiders on Thursday, Ryan McFadden of ESPN.com reports.

injuryReports.name: Daiyan Henley
injuryReports.returnComment: A trade involving Henley was agreed to Tuesday pending a physical, but the Broncos apparently found a red flag concerning his knee during that physical. Denver offered an updated trade to the Chargers with different draft compensation than the originally agreed upon 2027 fourth-round pick and 2028 fifth-round pick, but the two sides were unable to agree on an updated framework, so Henley will ultimately remain with the Chargers.
